proposed.name: Meaning in life
proposed.line: I don't know what my life is for.

alternatives.name: Meaning in life
alternatives.line: I don't know what my life is for.

why.detail: 58% of U.S. young adults said they lacked meaning or purpose in the previous month (Harvard Making Caring Common). In Great Britain, 9% of adults report low levels of feeling that what they do is worthwhile, 14% among those aged 16 to 29 (ONS).

sources.passage: Nearly 3 in 5 young adults (58%) reported that they lacked “meaning or purpose” in their lives in the previous month.
Almost 1 in 10 adults (9%) reported low levels of feeling that the things they do in life are worthwhile; this was more common among adults aged 16 to 29 years (14%) and 30 to 49 years (11%).

proposed.name: Reading

alternatives.name: Reading
alternatives.line: Reading forms, letters and instructions is hard for me.

why.detail: 28 percent of U.S. adults read at Level 1 or below, up from 19 percent in 2017 (NCES, PIAAC 2023). The OECD average is 26%.

sources.passage: Between 2017 and 2023, there were increases in the percentages of adults performing at the lowest proficiency level (Level 1 or below) in both literacy and numeracy: in literacy this percentage increased from 19 to 28 percent and in numeracy from 29 to 34 percent.
The average rate of literacy needs across the OECD is 26%

proposed.name: English
proposed.line: I don't speak English well enough to get by.

alternatives.name: English
alternatives.line: I don't speak English well enough to get by.

why.detail: In 2018-2022, 78.3% of U.S. residents age 5 and older spoke only English at home. Among those who spoke another language, 61.0% of Spanish speakers and 48.2% of Chinese speakers spoke English "very well" (Census ACS).

sources.passage: Over three-quarters (78.3%) of the nation age 5 and older spoke only English at home, according to newly released 2018-2022 American Community Survey (ACS), 5-year estimates.

Among the population age 5 and older that spoke a language other than English at home, 61.0% of Spanish speakers, 48.2% of Chinese speakers (which includes all dialects), and 69.8% of Tagalog (including Filipino) speakers spoke English “very well.”

proposed.line: I've spent so long looking after everyone else that I don't know what I want any more.

why.detail: Keeps the loss of self but shows what it looks like day to day: a life spent on other people's needs, and no answer when someone asks what you want. The name also matches the ID again.

why.detail: An area-style name so the Purpose heading doesn't mix problem and area labels, and a line that says what the putting off costs instead of only naming the habit.
